issues.legal_issue: The statutory scheme for prospecting and acquiring coal-bearing land applies to land that is not being worked when the relevant notice is issued, including mines worked in the past but then dormant.
material_facts: The mines had been worked in the past but mining operations had ceased for long periods before the prospecting notice.
One mine had ceased operating because it was considered uneconomical; the other had been closed after flooding.
The petitioners argued that the Act applied only to virgin land.
issues.conclusion: The Act applies to dormant collieries and other land not being worked when the notice is issued, even if mining had occurred there in the past; it is not limited to virgin land.
issues.legal_principle: The ordinary meaning of “unworked land” is land not being worked at the relevant time. A preamble may assist in resolving ambiguity, but clear statutory language governs; where the meaning is unclear, the preamble may explain it. The Court relied on In re the Kerala Education Bill, 1957, and on sections 4(1), 4(4), 5(b), 6, 7 and 8 of the Coal Bearing Areas (Acquisition and Development) Act, 1957. In particular, section 4(4)'s express exclusion for certain operations actually being carried on is consistent with the Act covering land whose operations have ceased.

rule.if: prospecting_notice_challenged and land_not_being_worked_when_notice_issued and (mine_worked_in_past or land_is_virgin)

predicates.prospecting_notice_challenged: A person challenges a notice issued to permit prospecting for a mineral in land.
predicates.land_not_being_worked_when_notice_issued: The land was not being worked for the mineral when the prospecting notice was issued.
predicates.mine_worked_in_past: Mining operations had taken place on the land before they ceased.
predicates.land_is_virgin: Mining operations had not previously taken place on the land.
predicates.statutory_scheme_applies_to_land: The statutory prospecting and acquisition scheme applies to the land.

issues.definition: If a prospecting notice is challenged and the land was not being worked when it was issued, the scheme applies whether the land was previously mined or was virgin.

issues.legal_issue: A prohibition on undertaking operations in notified land can prevent the resumption of mining after abandonment or discontinuance, but does not prevent resumption after a casual or ordinary-course closure.
material_facts: The mines had been closed for many years before the prospecting notice.
One petitioner had begun drilling before the notice but stopped after its publication.
The petitioners argued that “undertake” covered only beginning operations for the first time, not resuming operations.
issues.conclusion: “To undertake any operation” includes resuming an operation that was abandoned or discontinued, but does not capture resumption after a casual closure or a closure in the ordinary course of working a mine.
issues.legal_principle: Section 5(b) of the Coal Bearing Areas (Acquisition and Development) Act, 1957, bars a lessee from undertaking an operation in notified land while the notice remains in force. The Court interpreted “undertake” as entering upon work, and read the provision in light of section 16 of the Mines Act, 1952, and rules 3 and 7 of the Coal Mines Regulations, 1957, including the distinction between reopening after abandonment and ordinary interruptions in mining.

rule.if: prospecting_notice_challenged and lease_authorizes_mining and mining_operations_abandoned_or_discontinued and not closure_was_casual_or_ordinary

predicates.prospecting_notice_challenged: A person challenges the effect of a prospecting notice on mining operations in the notified land.
predicates.lease_authorizes_mining: A lease authorizes the holder to conduct mining operations on the land.
predicates.mining_operations_abandoned_or_discontin: Mining operations had ceased through abandonment or discontinuance before the proposed resumption.
predicates.closure_was_casual_or_ordinary: The interruption was a casual closure or a closure in the ordinary course of working the mine.
predicates.resumption_of_mining_is_barred: The holder cannot resume mining while the notice remains in force.

issues.definition: Where a prospecting notice affects a leased mine whose operations were abandoned or discontinued, resumption is barred unless the interruption was casual or part of ordinary mining operations.

issues.legal_issue: Land is excluded from a prospecting notice only to the extent that mining operations are actually being carried on in conformity with applicable law.
material_facts: One petitioner commenced drilling without having obtained the required permission and stopped after the notice was published.
The other petitioner had applied to reopen its mine but had not commenced operations because permission had not been received.
The petitioners relied on the statutory exclusion for land where operations were actually being carried on.
issues.conclusion: The statutory exclusion was unavailable because operations were not actually being carried on in conformity with applicable law; an authority's inaction on an application did not establish entitlement to the exclusion.
issues.legal_principle: Section 4(4) of the Coal Bearing Areas (Acquisition and Development) Act, 1957, excludes only the portion of land where coal-mining operations are actually being carried on in conformity with an enactment, rule or order. The Court applied the provision's plain language and held that an applicant could not rely on official inaction to satisfy it.

rule.if: prospecting_notice_challenged and exclusion_from_notice_claimed and (not operations_actually_underway or not operations_lawful)

predicates.prospecting_notice_challenged: A person challenges a prospecting notice covering land used or proposed for mining.
predicates.exclusion_from_notice_claimed: A person claims that some land must be excluded from the prospecting notice because mining is being carried on there.
predicates.operations_actually_underway: Mining operations were actually being carried on in the relevant portion of land when the notice was issued.
predicates.operations_lawful: The operations being carried on complied with applicable legal requirements.
predicates.land_not_excluded_from_notice: The relevant land does not qualify for exclusion from the prospecting notice.

issues.definition: A claimed exclusion fails if mining was not actually underway or was not lawful when the notice was issued.

issues.legal_issue: A temporary restriction preventing mining during the period required for prospecting is not an unreasonable restriction on the right to carry on business.
material_facts: The notice prevented mining in the affected land for up to two years, with a possible extension of up to one additional year.
The petitioners contended that this period was too long to be reasonable.
Prospecting required prolonged operations, and the petitioners did not state what shorter period would be reasonable.
issues.conclusion: The restrictions imposed by the Act were not unreasonable and did not contravene Article 19(1)(g).
issues.legal_principle: Article 19(1)(g), read with the authority to impose reasonable restrictions in the interests of the general public under Article 19(6), permits a restriction of the duration reasonably needed for prospecting. The Court considered the nature and duration of prospecting and the absence of any pleaded alternative reasonable period.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_business_res: A person challenges a restriction on mining as an infringement of the right to carry on business.
predicates.restriction_lasts_for_prospecting: The restriction prevents mining while prospecting is undertaken.
predicates.prospecting_operations_require_prolonged: The prospecting operations reasonably require an extended period to complete.
predicates.challenger_identifies_no_reasonable_shor: The challenger does not identify a shorter period that would reasonably allow the prospecting to be completed.
predicates.business_restriction_is_not_unreasonable: The restriction is not unreasonable as a limit on the right to carry on business.

issues.definition: A restriction lasting for the time reasonably needed for prolonged prospecting is not unreasonable where the challenger identifies no reasonable shorter period.

issues.legal_issue: A temporary restriction on rights under a mineral lease is a modification of those rights and is protected from the specified constitutional challenge by the constitutional protection for laws modifying mineral-searching or mineral-winning rights.
material_facts: The notice and the statutory prohibition prevented the petitioners from working their mines for a limited period.
The petitioners argued that a temporary suspension of their rights was not a modification of those rights.
The disputed rights arose under mining leases.
issues.conclusion: The temporary restriction modified the petitioners' lease rights, and Article 31A(1)(e) barred a challenge to sections 4 and 5 on the ground that they infringed Article 31(2).
issues.legal_principle: Article 31A(1)(e) protects laws providing for the modification of rights under agreements, leases or licences for searching for or winning minerals from challenges based on the specified constitutional rights. “Modification” includes alteration, limitation or restriction and need not be permanent. The Court distinguished Thakur Raghbir Singh v. Court of Wards, Ajmer, and relied on Sri Ram Ram Narain Medhi v. State of Bombay, Atma Ram v. State of Punjab, and In re Delhi Laws Act, 1912, in considering the meaning of modification and the limited scope of the earlier decision.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_temporary_mi: A person challenges a temporary restriction on rights held under an agreement, lease or licence for mineral exploration or extraction.
predicates.restriction_alters_lease_rights: The restriction limits or otherwise alters the holder's rights under the mineral agreement, lease or licence.
predicates.restriction_is_temporary: The restriction applies for a limited period rather than permanently.
predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_restriction_: The specified constitutional challenge to the restriction cannot be maintained.

issues.definition: A temporary restriction that alters rights under a mineral agreement, lease or licence is treated as a modification, so the specified constitutional challenge is barred.

issues.legal_issue: Acquisition provisions are not invalid merely because the compensation principles exclude the value of minerals, where the statute provides principles and a method for determining compensation and the minerals are not a separate tenement.
material_facts: The Act provided compensation for acquired land and specified principles and a method for determining it.
The Act excluded the value of minerals in calculating compensation.
The petitioners argued that mineral rights were separate from surface rights and required separate compensation.
The Court found that the petitioners held the minerals together with the land, not as a separate tenement.
issues.conclusion: The challenge to the acquisition provisions failed because the Act specified principles and a method for determining compensation, and an objection that the resulting compensation was inadequate could not be raised under Article 31(2).
issues.legal_principle: Article 31(2) requires a law authorizing compulsory acquisition to provide compensation and either fix its amount or specify the principles and manner for determining and giving it; such a law cannot be challenged on the ground that the compensation is inadequate. Sections 13 and 14 of the Coal Bearing Areas (Acquisition and Development) Act, 1957, supplied the compensation principles and method. The exclusion of mineral value was treated as an objection to adequacy, and the minerals were not a separate tenement in these cases.

predicates.challenge_to_compulsory_acquisition: A person challenges a law authorizing compulsory acquisition of property.
predicates.statute_provides_compensation_principles: The law provides principles and a method for determining and giving compensation for the acquired property.
predicates.mineral_rights_are_not_separate_tenement: The mineral rights are held with the land rather than as a separate property interest.
predicates.objection_is_that_compensation_is_inadeq: The challenge rests on the contention that the compensation provided is insufficient, including because it omits mineral value.
predicates.acquisition_challenge_based_on_compensat: The acquisition law cannot be invalidated on the ground that the compensation provided is inadequate.

issues.definition: Where the law supplies compensation principles and a method, and mineral rights are not a separate property interest, an objection that compensation is inadequate does not invalidate the acquisition law.
